newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl calls on SPD to agree German pension reform.
newsitem.headline: Kohl calls on SPD to agree German pension reform.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Monday called on the opposition Social Democratic (SPD) party to back a planned reform of Germany's pensions system.

Speaking before a meeting of his Christian Democrat party (CDU), Kohl said both parties should be prepared to make compromises on the reform, which under current proposals would see a small reduction in pensions.
"There is no way however that the legislation on both pension and (a separate) tax reform will not bear our imprint," Kohl told German television.

Kohl's government is anxious to introduce a plan which would eventually reduce a typical pension to 64 percent of average net wages from around 70 percent now in a bid to cope with the country's ageing population.
The package does not need the agreement of the SPD, which has sharply criticised the proposals and threatened to turn the issue into a key 1998 campaign issue.
It is due to announce on Monday whether it will enter talks with the government on the pension reform.

SPD social affairs expert Rudolf Dressler said before the decision was due that an earlier offer by the German Labour Minister Norbert Bluem to discuss alternative SPD proposals was not to be taken seriously.

According to Bild mass-circulation daily, Bluem said the government would be ready to reassess the planned pension cuts if the SPD could come up with other ways of reducing the cost of the system to those contributing towards it.
